result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is a tree. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4056-L4138){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_tree() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A tree is a connected, acyclic, undirected graph. For a graph with *n* nodes to be a tree it: - must be undirected - must be connected (single component) - must have exactly *n - 1* edges - must be acyclic ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if graph is a tree, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} For directed graphs, use `is_arborescence()` instead. For disconnected forests, use `is_forest()`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A connected, acyclic, undirected graph -- like this path -- qualifies as a tree: ::: {#018def38 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec tree = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) tree.is_tree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Closing the path into a cycle violates the "acyclic" requirement: ::: {#c18b0d53 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} cycle = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "A") ) cycle.is_tree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Leaving a node unconnected violates the "connected" requirement instead: ::: {#d86a44b7 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} disconnected = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") # isolated -- no edge connects it .add_edge("A", "B") ) disconnected.is_tree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Generated structures like star graphs are trees too, since they're connected and have exactly `n - 1` edges: ::: {#b08501ea .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} star = ec.Graph(directed=False) star.add_star_graph(n=5) star.is_tree() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` True ``` ::: :::
